newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Parsons gets Kuwait oil project work - official.
newsitem.headline: Parsons gets Kuwait oil project work - official.

text.p: Parsons Engineering Corp of the United States signed on Saturday a 24 million dinar ($80 million) project management contract to assist Kuwait Oil Co (KOC) develop crude oil production capacity, an oil official said.
KOC, the crude oil-producing arm of state-owned Kuwait Petroleum Corporation (KPC), will put its signature to the contract on Sunday, the official said.
The contract was signed on Saturday on behalf of Parsons Engineering by Dennis Pisula, vice-president, business development, of Parsons unit Parsons Process Group.
The contract will run for five years from December 1996. The work was priced on a cost plus fixed fee basis, the official, who declined to be identified, said by telephone.

The project management role, assisting KOC develop and expand oil output capacity, is central to Kuwait's long-term plans to raise capacity to 3.5 million barrels per day (bpd) by the year 2005 from almost 2.5 million at the moment.
Parsons was competing against America's International Bechtel, ABB Lummus Global and Foster Wheeler Corp.
Parsons is also the holder of the current KOC project management contract.

Oil officials say Parsons had agreed to a request by KOC that the life of the existing contract be extended to December 13 from its previous expiry date of September 13 to allow more time for KOC to choose a successor.
